content:
Reddit has announced two upcoming changes that some long-time users may not be happy about.

The company has already imposed one limitation on old Reddit, and is now announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support is being discontinued...

Old Reddit

Reddit significantly changed its user interface in 2018, drawing strong backlash from users who preferred the original. In response to those voices, the platform pledged at the time that, as long as people still used it, it would continue to provide access to what later became known as "old Reddit."

In August this year, the company first modified this policy, requiring old Reddit users to log in first. It is now further announcing that the original interface will be restricted to users who have used it within the past six months, with new users unable to access it.

Reddit says both measures are designed to reduce the company's scraping by AI (though if the company is willing to pay, that seems to be no problem).

RSS Feeds Will Be Discontinued

The discontinuation of RSS feeds is being explained for the same reason.

This change may be particularly inconvenient for subreddits that rely on RSS for their moderation workflows. Reddit says it understands this issue and suggests moderators use Devvit apps like Discord Relay.

Users React Unenthusiastically

Just reading the posts in the comments section makes it clear that a good number of long-time users are very unhappy with the latest developments.

What do you think of these latest changes? Feel free to share in the comments section.
